Below is a concise write‑up of what went wrong, why you saw those three errors, the minimal YAML fixes for each group, and finally a battery of “smoke‑tests” plus some CI‑level checks you can add so you never ship these mistakes again. --- ## 1. Diagnosis of Each Error | **Error Type** | **Observed** | **Root cause in config** | **Why that triggers the error** | |:--------------:|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **#1 Azure** | ``` APIConnectionError - Azure OpenAI request failed Details: {"error":{"code":"DeploymentNotFound","message":"The API deployment for this resource does not exist…"}} Status: 404 ``` | You passed `model: azure/gpt-4` (and similarly `azure/gpt-4o-mini`) instead of the actual **deployment name** and did not tell the OpenAI client “this is Azure.”
Azure expects you to call by your deployment_id (the name you gave the model in the Azure portal) and to set `api_type: azure`. | Azure’s service tries to look up a deployment literally called `"azure/gpt-4"`. That fails → 404 DeploymentNotFound. You also never set `api_type: azure` so the Python client didn’t flip into Azure‑mode. | | **#2 Anthropic** | ``` BadRequestError - Anthropic API error Details: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"model: field required"}} Status: 400 ``` | Litellm saw `model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514` and split off “anthropic” as the provider (OK), but **you never told it the real model ID** (you kept the vendor prefix in the YAML). The Anthropic client ended up sending no `model` field at all. | The Anthropic HTTP API refuses to complete unless you supply `"model": ""` in the JSON body. Because the vendor prefix wasn’t stripped to produce a valid Anthropic model name, the client sent an empty body → 400 “model: field required.” | | **#3 Groq** | ``` BadRequestError - Groq API error Details: {"error":{"message":"max_tokens exceeds the model context window. Requested: 32768, Context window: 8192"}} Status: 400 ``` | You set `max_tokens: 32768` for Groq LLaMA variants, but those Groq backends only support an 8 k context window. | Groq’s API checks `max_tokens` against its hard cap of 8192 tokens → invalid_request_error because you asked for far too many tokens. | --- ## 2. The Minimal Fixes Below are **only** the lines that change in your YAML. (Assuming your aliases/indentation remain the same.) --- ### 🔧 Group B (Azure OpenAI) ```diff - model_name: azure-gpt4 litellm_params: - model: azure/gpt-4 + api_type: azure + deployment_id: gpt-4 api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com api_version: "2024-02-15-preview" max_tokens: 4096 - model_name: azure-gpt4-mini litellm_params: - model: azure/gpt-4o-mini + api_type: azure + deployment_id: gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: https://contoso.openai.azure.com api_version: "2024-02-15-preview" max_tokens: 4096 ``` > **What changed?** > 1. Added `api_type: azure` so the OpenAI‑python client flips into Azure mode. > 2. Swapped out `model:` for your actual Azure deployment name via `deployment_id:`. --- ### 🔧 Group C (Anthropic) ```diff - model_name: claude-opus litellm_params: - model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514 + model: claude-opus-4-20250514 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 4096 - model_name: claude-sonnet litellm_params: - model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514 + model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 4096 ``` > **What changed?** > We drop the `anthropic/` vendor prefix in the `model:` line so that the Anthropic client sees exactly the model ID it expects. --- ### 🔧 Group E (Groq) ```diff - model_name: llama-fast litellm_params: - max_tokens: 32768 + max_tokens: 8192 - model_name: llama-mini litellm_params: - max_tokens: 32768 + max_tokens: 8192 ``` > **What changed?** > We reduced the `max_tokens` to the Groq context‑window limit (8 k) so the request will be accepted. --- ## 3. Validation Checklist After you apply those fixes, run through these quick checks before you call it “done”: | Step | Command / Action | Expected result | |:----:|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | ➊ | `litellm config validate litellm_config.yaml` | No schema errors | | ➋ | `litellm healthcheck` | All registered providers respond “OK” (no 4xx/5xx) | | ➌ | `litellm run --model azure-gpt4 --prompt "Hi"` | Returns a 200 OK completion from your Azure deployment | | ➍ | `litellm run --model claude-opus --prompt "Hello"` | Returns a 200 OK completion from Anthropic | | ➎ | `litellm run --model llama-fast --prompt "Test"` | Returns a 200 OK completion from Groq | | ➏ | Spot‑check logs to confirm **no** more 4xx DeploymentNotFound / model‑required | Your tails‑end logs should be clean. | --- ## 4. Preventing This in CI Below are a few lightweight checks you can add to your pre‑merge pipeline so these mistakes never slip through again: | **Check** | **Why** | |:-----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **1. Schema + lint validation** | `litellm config validate` + a YAML linter (`yamllint`). Catches indentation, required keys. | | **2. Azure deployment lookup** | A tiny Python snippet (or Azure CLI) that verifies each `deployment_id` exists under the resource. | | **3. Vendor‑prefix rule** | Static lint: if you see `model: anthropic/...` or `model: azure/...`, fail build. | | **4. Context‑window sanity check** | CI script that reads `max_tokens` and fails if it exceeds known limits (e.g. Groq ≤ 8192). | | **5. Automatic smoke tests** | Run `litellm run --model …` for at least one model in each group (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Groq). | By combining schema validation, a quick deployment/credential lookup, plus one-shot smoke tests, you’ll have 100% confidence that: - your Azure deployments exist and you’re calling them correctly, - your Anthropic models are named properly, - you never overshoot the token window, - and you won’t ship an “oops, forgot the provider” in your config again. --- **That’s it** – apply the three tiny diffs above, run the six validation steps, add the CI lint + smoke‑test guards, and you’ll never see those three errors in your LiteLLM logs again. 🚀
